text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Coast politician Emmanuel Maitha is arrested in Mombasa as the bodies of three policemen missing in action are recovered.
- Constitutional reform talks between the government, the civic lobby group and the opposition will be launched on Tuesday.
- Twelve people suspected of taking part in the violence on Kenya's Indian Ocean coast deny charges of possessing offensive weapons.
- A religious committee brokering reform dialogue between the ruling Kenya African National Union party and the opposition abolish the position of coordinating chairman.
- A skirmish between the Maasai and the Kisii communities leaves one schoolboy dead and 19 people seriously injured.
- The local chapter of the Intenrational Commission of Jurists says Kenya cannot justify the existence of its security apparatus without providing security to all her citizens.
- More than 200 people fleeing violence in Mombasa arrive in Nairobi as three more people are reportedly killed in the coast region.
- More than 700 slum dwellers at Mathare in Nairobi are rendered homeless as fire razes their houses.
- Mobil Oil Kenya Limited raises its fuel prices by about eight percent effective from Tuesday. ($1=69.99 Kenyan shillings)
